⏺ I've stopped and won't run anything else until you say so. Your two
  notices are about Ruflo, so I'll cover those first, then the
  LosslessCut review.

  The two Ruflo mods

  These are trust notices: Ruflo telling you what each mod is allowed
  to do. They don't show that either mod did anything wrong. Both
  come from the Ruflo / claude-flow setup your ~/CLAUDE.md installs.
  They're also why every message you send gets a "Routing task …
  Agent: reviewer" block added to it.

  What the permissions mean in practice:

  Permission: process.run (both mods)
  What it allows: Run any shell command as you, without going through

  me.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Permission: on tool.call (both mods)
  What it allows: See, change or answer any tool call I make. A mod
  could edit a command before it runs or hand back made-up output.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Permission: on * (ruflo-swarm)
  What it allows: See every event in the session: your prompts, file
  paths, command output. Here that includes the file names in your
  private video folder.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Permission: http.fetch (ruflo-console)
  What it allows: Send network requests. With the permissions above,
  it could send what it sees out of your machine.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Permission: on tool.check (ruflo-console)
  What it allows: Answer permission prompts itself. This is the most
  serious one. It can approve actions that would normally stop and
  ask you, so the permission prompt you just used doesn't fully
  protect you while this mod is loaded.
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Permission: on plugin.register (ruflo-console)
  What it allows: Block other mods from loading, including security
  ones.

  Things this session showed:
  - Ruflo writes files wherever you start a session. It created
    .claude-flow/mods/session.json inside your video folder at 00:57.
    If you start sessions in private folders, expect them to collect
    Ruflo state files.
  - The mods load even when Ruflo's tool server doesn't. That server
    timed out at startup today, so these permissions apply even when
    you aren't using Ruflo's tools.
  - Nothing looked tampered with. In principle a mod with tool.call
    could have changed the results I saw. Nothing this session
    suggested it did, but I can't rule it out from inside the
    session.

  My recommendation: turn off ruflo-console unless you actively use
  it. Approving permission prompts plus network access plus the power
  to block other mods is a lot to give a tool you don't need. Keep
  ruflo-swarm only if you actually run swarms. I don't know Ruflo's
  exact command for turning off a mod and won't guess one. /plugin is
  the first place to look. If you'd like, I can find where they're
  turned on using read-only commands, but only once you OK that.

  LosslessCut review

  I found nothing that should block you. I compared your current
  config.json with the backup LosslessCut saved on Sep 11:

  - Most of the change is LosslessCut's own update. About 60 of the
    changed lines are key bindings converted to the new key-naming
    format ("k" became "KeyK"), which version 3.69 does
    automatically.
  - Your setting changes are safer than before:
    - LosslessCut now confirms before exporting and asks before
      closing.
    - Moving temp files to the Trash after export, and closing the
      file after export, are both off now.
    - The source file's date is no longer copied to the output as its
      start time.
  - Low-risk notes:
    - Possibly lost shortcut: the update dropped the Escape →
      close-dialog shortcut. I couldn't confirm whether Escape is now
      built in. My search of the app for that was still running in
      the background when you stopped me, so I have no result. If
      Escape stops closing dialogs, add the binding back.
    - Overwrite is on: enableOverwriteOutput: true is set, and
      exports go into the same folder as the source videos. Each
      output name includes the cut times, so only a repeat export of
      the exact same range gets replaced. Your original videos aren't
      at risk.
    - Output is fixed to MP4: outFormatLocked: "mp4". That's fine for
      this folder. Exports from MKV files with subtitles or unusual
      audio could fail.

  ⎿  # Chrome DevTools for agents

     [![npm chrome-devtools-mcp
     package](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/chrome-devtools-mcp.s
     vg)](https://npmjs.org/package/chrome-devtools-mcp)

     Chrome DevTools for agents (`chrome-devtools-mcp`) lets
     your coding agent (such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor or
     Copilot)
     control and inspect a live Chrome browser. It acts as a
     Model-Context-Protocol
     (MCP) server, giving your AI coding assistant access to the
     full power of
     Chrome DevTools for reliable automation, in-depth
     debugging, and performance analysis.
     A [CLI][cli] is also provided for use without MCP.

     [Tool reference][tool-reference] | [Changelog][changelog] |
     [Contributing][contributing] |
     [Troubleshooting][troubleshooting] | [Design
     Principles][design-principles]

     ## Key features

     - **Get performance insights**: Uses [Chrome
       DevTools](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-fron
     tend) to record
       traces and extract actionable performance insights.
     - **Advanced browser debugging**: Analyze network requests,
     take screenshots and
       check browser console messages (with source-mapped stack
     traces).
     - **Reliable automation**. Uses
       [puppeteer](https://github.com/puppeteer/puppeteer) to
     automate actions in
       Chrome and automatically wait for action results.

     ## Disclaimers

     `chrome-devtools-mcp` exposes content of the browser
     instance to the MCP clients
     allowing them to inspect, debug, and modify any data in the
     browser or DevTools.
     Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information that you
     don't want to share with
     MCP clients.

     `chrome-devtools-mcp` officially supports Google Chrome and
     [Chrome for Testing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chr
     ome-for-testing/) only.
     Other Chromium-based browsers may work, but this is not
     guaranteed, and you may encounter unexpected behavior. Use
     at your own discretion.
     We are committed to providing fixes and support for the
     latest version of [Extended Stable
     Chrome](https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/schedule).

     Performance tools may send trace URLs to the Google CrUX
     API to fetch real-user
     experience data. This helps provide a holistic performance
     picture by
     presenting field data alongside lab data. This data is
     collected by the [Chrome
     User Experience Report
     (CrUX)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux). To disable
     this, run with the `--no-performance-crux` flag.

     ## **Usage statistics**

     Google collects usage statistics (such as tool invocation
     success rates, latency, and environment information) to
     improve the reliability and performance of Chrome DevTools
     MCP.

     Data collection is **enabled by default**. You can opt-out
     by passing the `--no-usage-statistics` flag when starting
     the server:

     ```json
     "args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest",
     "--no-usage-statistics"]
     ```

     Google handles this data in accordance with the [Google
     Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy).

     Google's collection of usage statistics for Chrome DevTools
     MCP is independent from the Chrome browser's usage
     statistics. Opting out of Chrome metrics does not
     automatically opt you out of this tool, and vice-versa.

     Collection is disabled if
     `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS` or `CI` env
     variables are set.

     ## Update checks

     By default, the server periodically checks the npm registry
     for updates and logs a notification when a newer version
     is available.
     You can disable these update checks by setting the
     `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS` environment
     variable.

     ## Requirements

     - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/)
     [LTS](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule)
     version.
     - [Chrome](https://www.google.com/chrome/) current stable
     version or newer.
     - [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/)

     ## Getting started

     Add the following config to your MCP client:

     ```json
     {
       "mcpServers": {
         "chrome-devtools": {
           "command": "npx",
           "args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"]
         }
       }
     }
     ```

     > [!NOTE]
     > Using `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest` ensures that your MCP
     client will always use the latest version of the Chrome
     DevTools MCP server.

     If you are interested in doing only basic browser tasks,
     use the `--slim` mode:

     ```json
     {
       "mcpServers": {
         "chrome-devtools": {
           "command": "npx",
           "args": ["-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest",
     "--slim", "--headless"]
         }
       }
     }
     ```

     See [Slim tool reference][slim-tool-reference].

     ### MCP Client configuration

     For setup instructions specific to your editor or agent
     (e.g. Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code), please
     see our [Client Configurations
     Guide][client-configurations-guide].

     ### Your first prompt

     Enter the following prompt in your MCP Client to check if
     everything is working:

     ```
     Check the performance of https://developers.chrome.com
     ```

     Your MCP client should open the browser and record a
     performance trace.

     > [!NOTE]
     > The MCP server will start the browser automatically once
     the MCP client uses a tool that requires a running browser
     instance. Connecting to the Chrome DevTools MCP server on
     its own will not automatically start the browser.

     ## Tools

     If you run into any issues, checkout our [troubleshooting
     guide][troubleshooting].
     See the full [Tool Reference][tool-reference] for a
     complete list of all supported MCP capabilities.

     ## Configuration

     Find the complete list of server parameters (e.g.,
     `--headless`, `--isolated`, `--slim`) and how to configure
     WebSocket connections in the [Configuration
     Guide][configuration-guide].

     ## Advanced Usage

     For advanced features such as handling concurrent sessions,
     persistent user data directories, connecting to a running
     Chrome instance instead of starting a new one, or debugging
     on Android, see our [Advanced Usage
     Guide][advanced-usage-guide].

     ## Integrating as a browser subagent

     If you are developing agentic tooling and want to provide
     an integrated browser subagent as part of your product, we
     recommend building on top of Chrome DevTools for agents.

     For a reference implementation, see the [Gemini CLI browser
     agent documentation](https://geminicli.com/docs/core/subag
     ents/#browser-agent).

  ⎿  ## fileNavigations
       Set to false to disallow navigating to file: URLs. When
     disabled, new_page, navigate_page and the slim navigate
     tool reject file: URLs, including view-source: URLs that
     target them. This restricts navigations the server
     performs. It is not a filesystem sandbox: it does not
     affect pages the browser already had open when the server
     connected, and the browser can reach the filesystem by
     other means. Use OS sandboxing for full filesystem
     confinement.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `true`

     - **`--sourceMaps`/ `--source-maps`**
     ## isolated
       If specified, creates a temporary user-data-dir that is
     automatically cleaned up after the browser is closed.
     Defaults to false.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `false`

     - **`--userDataDir`/ `--user-data-dir`**
     ## usageStatistics
       Set to false to opt-out of usage statistics collection.
     Google collects usage data to improve the tool, handled
     under the Google Privacy Policy
     (https://policies.google.com/privacy). This is independent
     from Chrome browser metrics. Disabled if
     `CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_USAGE_STATISTICS` or `CI` env
     variables are set.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `true`

     - **`--javascriptEvaluation`/ `--javascript-evaluation`**
     ## performanceCrux
       Set to false to disable sending URLs from performance
     traces to CrUX API to get field performance data.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `true`

     - **`--usageStatistics`/ `--usage-statistics`**
     ## slim
       Exposes a "slim" set of 3 tools covering navigation,
     script execution and screenshots only. Useful for basic
     browser tasks.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `false`

     - **`--redactNetworkHeaders`/ `--redact-network-headers`**
     ## redactNetworkHeaders
       If true, redacts some of the network headers considered
     sensitive before returning to the client.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `false`

     - **`--allowUnrestrictedPaths`/
     `--allow-unrestricted-paths`**
     ## filesystemRoot
       A directory that filesystem tools are allowed to access.
     May be specified more than once.
       - **Type:** array
       - **Default:** `OS temp directory`

     - **`--config`**
     ## categoryMemory
       Set to false to exclude tools related to memory.
       - **Type:** boolean
       - **Default:** `true`

     - **`--categoryExperimentalWebmcp`/
     `--category-experimental-webmcp`**

       <summary>Claude Code</summary>

     **Install via CLI (MCP only)**

     Use the Claude Code CLI to add the Chrome DevTools MCP
     server (<a
     href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp">guide</a>):

     ```bash
     claude mcp add chrome-devtools --scope user npx
     chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
     ```

     **Install as a Plugin (MCP + Skills)**

     > [!NOTE]
     > If you already had Chrome DevTools MCP installed
     previously for Claude Code, make sure to remove it first
     from your installation and configuration files.

     To install Chrome DevTools MCP with skills, add the
     marketplace registry in Claude Code:

     ```sh
     /plugin marketplace add ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp
     ```

     Then, install the plugin:

     144+) running locally from the user data directory identified by

       43 <h1>Where your tokens go before you type anything</h
          1>
       44 <p class="lede">A detailed guide to the four sources
           that loaded about 88,000 tokens into a session befo
          re any work happened. For each one: what it is, how
          it loads, what it costs (measured where possible), e
          xamples, configuration, and how to trim it safely an
          d reversibly.</p>
       45
       46 <div class="card">
       47 <b>How to read the numbers.</b>
       48 <span class="tag measured">measured</span> = counted
           from files or the session counter on 2026-10-05.
       49 <span class="tag estimate">estimate</span> = derived
           (characters ÷ 4, or counted from the session's tool
           list).
       50 <span class="tag done">done</span> = already changed
           today. Run <code>/context</code> in a fresh session
           for exact numbers by category; it is the ground tru
          th and replaces every estimate here.
       51 </div>
       52

       69 <h2 id="big-picture">1. The big picture</h2>
       70
       71 <p>Claude Code rebuilds its context at the start of
          every request. Before your message is read, it assem
          bles a system prompt, tool definitions, and several
          <em>discovery lists</em>: one entry per agent, per s
          kill, and per MCP tool, so the model knows what exis
          ts and can choose it. Each entry is short, but there
           are hundreds, and they are paid for on <strong>ever
          y request</strong>. Prompt caching makes repeats che
          aper, but the space still counts against the context
           window.</p>
       72
       73 <div class="mermaid">
       74 flowchart TB
       75   subgraph Always["Loaded on every request"]
       76     SP["System prompt + built-in tools<br/>(fixed, ~
          20k)"]
       77     AG["Agent list<br/>298 files → ~200 entries"]
       78     SK["Skill list<br/>~450 entries"]
       79     MC["MCP tool names + server instructions<br/>~60
          0 deferred names"]
       80     IN["Instruction files<br/>CLAUDE.md ×2, rules ×2
          , MEMORY.md"]
       81     HK["Hook output<br/>(output style, status lines)
          "]
       82   end
       83   subgraph OnDemand["Loaded only when used"]
       84     TS["Full MCP tool schemas<br/>(fetched via ToolS
          earch)"]
       85     SB["Skill bodies<br/>(loaded when a skill is inv
          oked)"]
       86     AB["Agent prompts<br/>(only inside a spawned age
          nt)"]
       87   end
       88   You["Your message"] --> Ctx
       89   SP & AG & SK & MC & IN & HK --> Ctx(("Context<br/>
          ~88k before work"))
       90   Ctx --> Model["Model reply"]
       91   Model -. "uses a tool / skill" .-> OnDemand
       92 </div>
       93
       94 <h3>The 88k measurement</h3>
       95 <p><span class="tag measured">measured</span> The se
          ssion's remaining-token counter fell from 15,000,000
           to 14,911,596 on the first tool call, a drop of <b>
          88,404</b>. Almost all of that was setup: the user m
          essage and one short command were tiny. The rest of
          the session added about 30k, mostly config files and
           logs printed into the conversation.</p>
       96

       98 <tr><th>Source</th><th class="n">Approx. tokens</th>
          <th>Basis</th><th>Can you trim it?</th></tr>

          d class="n">~20k</td><td><span class="tag estimate">
          estimate</span> June <code>/context</code>: 4.1k pro

          eline</td></tr>
      100 <tr><td><b>Agent list</b></td><td class="n">~14–20k<
          /td><td><span class="tag measured">measured</span> 5
          6,918 description chars ≈ 14.2k, plus names and tool

      101 <tr><td><b>Skill list</b></td><td class="n">~12k</td
          ><td><span class="tag estimate">estimate</span> ~450
           entries × ~25 tokens (descriptions truncated)</td><
          td>Yes</td></tr>
      102 <tr><td><b>Connectors / MCP names + instructions</b>
          </td><td class="n">~10–14k</td><td><span class="tag

      106 <p>These add up to roughly 64–76k. The rest of the 8

          ll close the gap.</p>

      120 <h2 id="agents">2. Source 1: Agent list</h2>
      121
      122 <h3>What it is</h3>
      123 <p>Every <code>.md</code> file with frontmatter unde
          r <code>~/.claude/agents/</code> (searched recursive
          ly) becomes a <em>subagent type</em>. Claude Code li
          sts each one in the Agent tool's description (name,
          description, tool list) so the model can choose one
          to delegate to. The full agent prompt (the body of t
          he file) is <b>not</b> loaded until that agent is ac
          tually spawned. The cost is the <b>description</b> f
          ield, multiplied by the number of agents.</p>
      124
      125 <h3>How it's wired on this machine</h3>
      126 <div class="mermaid">
      127 flowchart LR
      128   A["~/.claude/agents"] -- symlink --> B["~/.agent-s
          kills/agents<br/>(canonical, 298 .md files)"]
      129   B --> T["top level: 110"]
      130   B --> I["_incoming/: 88<br/>⚠ staging folder, load
          ed live"]
      131   B --> C["3-contains-studio/: 35"]
      132   B --> M["5-misc-personal/: 20"]
      133   B --> O["1-eng-specialist-pack 11 · skill-porter 1
          1<br/>2-personal-tooled 9 · 6-automation-workbench 6
          <br/>commands 4 · skill-creator 2 · others 2"]
      134   S["~/.claude/skills"] -- symlink --> P["~/.agent-s
          kills/active-skills<br/>(curated projection, 300)"]
      135   style I fill:#fde2e4,stroke:#c2185b
      136 </div>
      137 <p>Note the asymmetry: <b>skills</b> already go thro
          ugh a curated projection (<code>active-skills</code>
          ), but <b>agents</b> point at the full canonical lib
          rary. Everything in the library, including the <code
          >_incoming</code> staging folder, is live.</p>
      138
      139 <h3>Measured facts <span class="tag measured">measur
          ed</span></h3>
      140 <table>
      141 <tr><th>Metric</th><th class="n">Value</th></tr>
      142 <tr><td>Agent <code>.md</code> files</td><td class="
          n">298</td></tr>
      143 <tr><td>Files with a frontmatter <code>name:</code><
          /td><td class="n">278</td></tr>
      144 <tr><td>Unique agent names</td><td class="n">198</td
          ></tr>
      145 <tr><td>Names defined more than once</td><td class="
          n">77</td></tr>
      146 <tr><td>Files in <code>_incoming/</code> (staging)</
          td><td class="n">88</td></tr>
      147 <tr><td>Total description characters</td><td class="
          n">56,918 (≈14.2k tokens)</td></tr>
      148 <tr><td>Agents with <code>&lt;example&gt;</code> blo
          cks in the description</td><td class="n">7</td></tr>
      149 </table>
      150
      151 <h3>Examples: the most expensive descriptions</h3>
      152 <table>
      153 <tr><th>Agent</th><th class="n">Desc. chars</th><th>
          Why it's large</th></tr>
      154 <tr><td><code>feedback-synthesizer</code> (×2: top l
          evel <b>and</b> 3-contains-studio)</td><td class="n"
          >1,842 each</td><td>Four inline example dialogues</t
          d></tr>
      155 <tr><td><code>_incoming/templates/base-template-gene
          rator</code></td><td class="n">1,410</td><td>Two exa
          mple blocks; staging copy</td></tr>
      156 <tr><td><code>6-automation-workbench/*</code> (5 age
          nts)</td><td class="n">1,098–1,170</td><td>Two examp
          les + a "do not use" clause each</td></tr>
      157 <tr><td><code>agent-consolidate</code></td><td class
          ="n">642</td><td>Two examples</td></tr>
      158 </table>
      159 <p>A typical lean description is 100–200 characters.
           One with examples is 5–10× that. Examples help rout
          ing when they're <em>distinctive</em>; most here res
          tate the description.</p>
      160
      161 <h3>Duplicates: what happens</h3>
      162 <p>Seventy-seven names appear more than once (for ex
          ample <code>backend-dev</code>, <code>code-reviewer<
          /code>, <code>content-creator</code>, <code>system-a
          rchitect</code>, <code>ecosystem-analyzer</code>). C
          laude Code keeps one definition per name, so duplica
          tes don't usually double the list. But <b>which copy
           wins is not something you control</b>, and two copi
          es can drift apart. You may edit one and get the oth
          er.</p>
      163
      164 <h3>Configuration: the agent file format</h3>
      165 <pre><code>---
      166 name: code-reviewer                 # unique id; bec
          omes subagent_type
      167 description: Review a diff for correctness and secur
          ity. Use after a major step.
      168 tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash       # optional; omit
           = all tools
      169 model: sonnet                       # optional
      170 ---
      171 System prompt for the agent goes here. It is ONLY lo
          aded when spawned,
      172 so length here costs nothing until use.</code></pre>
      173 <div class="callout"><b>Rule of thumb:</b> put the d
          etail in the <em>body</em> (free until used) and kee
          p the <code>description</code> to one or two sentenc
          es that say <em>when</em> to use the agent.</div>
      174
      175 <h3>How to trim it (reversible)</h3>
      176 <p><b>Option A: Agent projection (recommended).</b>
          Mirror what you already do for skills: build <code>~
          /.agent-skills/active-agents/</code> containing syml
          inks to the agents you actually use, then repoint <c
          ode>~/.claude/agents</code> at it. The canonical lib
          rary is untouched.</p>
      177 <pre><code># 1. Build the projection (symlinks only;
           canonical files untouched)
      178 mkdir -p ~/.agent-skills/active-agents
      179 for a in code-reviewer python-expert ecosystem-dev p
          review-first-operator \
      180          media-brief-to-shot-plan media-release-qa c
          oh-modder; do
      181   src=$(grep -rl "^name: *$a\$" ~/.agent-skills/agen
          ts --include=*.md | grep -v _incoming | head -1)
      182   [ -n "$src" ] &amp;&amp; ln -s "$src" ~/.agent-ski
          lls/active-agents/"$a".md
      183 done
      184
      185 # 2. Repoint (the old link target is recorded in the
           link itself; easy to restore)
      186 ln -sfn ~/.agent-skills/active-agents ~/.claude/agen
          ts
      187
      188 # Rollback
      189 ln -sfn ~/.agent-skills/agents ~/.claude/agents</cod
          e></pre>
      190 <p><b>Option B: Minimum change.</b> Move <code>_inco
          ming/</code> out of the live tree (88 files, about 3
          0% of the list): <code>mv ~/.agent-skills/agents/_in
          coming ~/.agent-skills/agents-incoming-2026-10-05</c
          ode>. Staging content shouldn't be routable anyway.<
          /p>
      191 <p><b>Option C: Shorten descriptions.</b> Move <code
          >&lt;example&gt;</code> blocks from <code>descriptio
          n</code> into the body. Same behavior when spawned,
          ~1.5k chars saved per agent.</p>
      192
      193 <!-- ===============================================
          ============= -->
      194 <h2 id="skills">3. Source 2: Skill list</h2>
      195
      196 <h3>What it is</h3>
      197 <p>A <b>skill</b> is a folder with a <code>SKILL.md<
          /code>. Claude Code lists each skill's name and a tr
          uncated description (cut off with "…" at about 80 ch
          aracters) so it can choose one. The body loads only
          when the skill is invoked. <b>Slash commands</b> (<c
          ode>.md</code> files in <code>~/.claude/commands/</c
          ode>) show up in the same list. Commands in subfolde
          rs become namespaced (<code>commands/sparc/coder.md<
          /code> → <code>sparc:coder</code>).</p>
      198
      199 <h3>Where the ~450 entries come from</h3>
      200 <div class="mermaid">
      201 flowchart LR
      202   L["Skill list<br/>~450 entries"]
      203   P1["~/.claude/skills → active-skills<br/>300 (of 3
          48 canonical)"] --> L
      204   P2["~/.claude/commands/<br/>167 files in 18 Ruflo
          folders"] --> L
      205   P3["Enabled plugins' skills<br/>(coderabbit, deskt
          op-commander,<br/>ruflo-swarm, built-ins…)"] --> L
      206   style P2 fill:#fde2e4,stroke:#c2185b
      207 </div>
      208
      209 <h3>Measured facts <span class="tag measured">measur
          ed</span></h3>
      210 <table>
      211 <tr><th>Source</th><th class="n">Count</th><th>Note<
          /th></tr>
      212 <tr><td><code>~/.agent-skills/active-skills</code> (
          the projection)</td><td class="n">300</td><td>Only 4
          8 fewer than the full 348; the projection barely tri
          ms</td></tr>
      213 <tr><td><code>~/.claude/commands/</code> Ruflo/claud
          e-flow folders</td><td class="n">167 files</td><td>I
          nstalled by <code>ruflo init</code>; now orphaned si
          nce Ruflo is disabled</td></tr>
      214 </table>
      215 <p>Breakdown of the 167 command files by folder:</p>
      216 <table>

      227 <h3>Examples</h3>
      228 <p>Many of these entries have no description and sho
          w up as a bare name (<code>sparc:coder</code>, <code
          >swarm:swarm-spawn</code>, <code>hive-mind:hive-mind
          -metrics</code>). They cost little each, but there a
          re 167 of them, they all point to tooling you just t
          urned off, and many overlap (<code>sparc:coder</code
          > vs <code>sparc:code</code>, <code>coordination:spa
          wn</code> vs <code>coordination:agent-spawn</code> v
          s <code>agents:spawn</code>).</p>

      230 <h3>Configuration: skill and command formats</h3>
      231 <pre><code># ~/.claude/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
      232 ---
      233 name: my-skill
      234 description: One line saying WHEN to use it. Only ~8
          0 chars show in the list.
      235 ---
      236 Full instructions. Loaded only when invoked.
      237
      238 # ~/.claude/commands/review/quick.md   →  appears as
            review:quick
      239 ---
      240 description: Quick read-only review of staged change
          s
      241 ---
      242 Review the staged diff and …</code></pre>
      243
      244 <h3>How to trim it (reversible)</h3>
      245 <pre><code># Archive the 18 Ruflo command folders +
          3 root files (move, never delete)
      246 ARCH=~/.claude/commands-archive-ruflo-2026-10-05
      247 mkdir -p "$ARCH"
      248 cd ~/.claude/commands
      249 mv agents analysis automation coordination github hi
          ve-mind hooks memory \
      250    monitoring optimization pair sparc stream-chain s
          warm training truth \
      251    verify workflows claude-flow-help.md claude-flow-
          memory.md \
      252    claude-flow-swarm.md "$ARCH"/
      253 # keep agmsg.md (yours, not Ruflo's)
      254
      255 # Rollback
      256 mv ~/.claude/commands-archive-ruflo-2026-10-05/* ~/.
          claude/commands/</code></pre>
      257 <p>Then tighten the skill projection: 300 of 348 mea
          ns nearly everything is active. Use the June audit's
           categories (§3 there) to drop clusters you don't us
          e day to day, such as the ToolUniverse/devtu science
           skills, ML training (axolotl, torchtitan, trl, gguf
          ), and the many overlapping video generators. Remove
           the symlinks from <code>active-skills</code>; the c
          anonical files stay.</p>

      260 <h2 id="connectors">4. Source 3: Connectors and MCP
          tool names</h2>
      261
      262 <h3>What it is</h3>
      263 <p>MCP servers provide tools. In this setup, MCP too
          ls are <b>deferred</b>: only the <em>names</em> are
          listed each request, and a tool's full schema is fet
          ched with ToolSearch when it's needed. Each server c
          an also inject an <b>instructions block</b> into the
           system prompt. That's paid every request, even if y
          ou never use the server.</p>
      264 <p>There are three kinds here:</p>
      265 <ul>
      266 <li><b>claude.ai connectors</b>: integrations you co
          nnected on claude.ai (Airtable, Canva, Notion…). Bec
          ause you sign in to Claude Code with that account, t
          hey come along into the terminal too.</li>
      267 <li><b>Local MCP servers</b>: configured in <code>~/
          .claude.json</code> (e.g. <code>claude-terminal</cod
          e>, <code>engram</code>, now <code>chrome-devtools</
          code>).</li>
      268 <li><b>Plugin MCP servers</b>: provided by plugins (
          context7, desktop-commander).</li>
      269 </ul>
      270
      271 <h3>What was loaded this session <span class="tag es
          timate">estimate</span></h3>
      272 <table>
      273 <tr><th>Server</th><th class="n">Tool names</th><th>
          Instructions block?</th><th>Likely terminal use</th>
          </tr>

          50</td><td>—</td><td>Only if you drive Claude Termin
          al.app from here</td></tr>
      275 <tr><td>vidIQ</td><td class="n">~70</td><td>—</td><t
          d>Low (YouTube work is usually in the web app)</td><
          /tr>
      276 <tr><td>Airtable</td><td class="n">~46</td><td>Yes,
          long</td><td>Low</td></tr>
      277 <tr><td>Notion</td><td class="n">~45</td><td>Yes</td
          ><td>Medium</td></tr>
      278 <tr><td>Lovable</td><td class="n">~45</td><td>Yes, l
          ong</td><td>Low</td></tr>
      279 <tr><td>Canva</td><td class="n">~41</td><td>—</td><t
          d>Low</td></tr>
      280 <tr><td>artlist</td><td class="n">~32</td><td>Yes, v
          ery long</td><td>Medium (media work)</td></tr>
      281 <tr><td>Descript</td><td class="n">~15</td><td>Yes</
          td><td>Medium</td></tr>
      282 <tr><td>Engram</td><td class="n">14</td><td>Yes</td>
          <td>High (your memory system)</td></tr>
      283 <tr><td>Google Docs / Sheets / Slides</td><td class=
          "n">~15</td><td>Short</td><td>Low</td></tr>
      284 <tr><td>Claude Docs</td><td class="n">8</td><td>Yes,
           long</td><td>Low</td></tr>
      285 <tr><td>Indeed · Exa · Gemini</td><td class="n">~9</
          td><td>—</td><td>Low</td></tr>
      286 <tr><td>context7 (plugin)</td><td class="n">2</td><t
          d>Yes, short</td><td>High (library docs)</td></tr>
      287 </table>
      288 <p>About 600 names plus about 7 instruction blocks.
          A name like <code>mcp__claude_ai_Airtable__list_reco
          rds_for_table</code> is about 15 tokens, and there a
          re hundreds of them.</p>
      289
      290 <div class="mermaid">
      291 sequenceDiagram
      292   participant CC as Claude Code
      293   participant S as MCP server
      294   participant M as Model
      295   CC->>S: connect at startup
      296   S-->>CC: tool list + instructions
      297   CC->>M: every request: tool NAMES + instructions
      298   Note over M: cost paid even if unused
      299   M->>CC: ToolSearch("select:tool_x")
      300   CC->>M: full schema for tool_x only
      301   M->>CC: call tool_x
      302   CC->>S: execute
      303 </div>
      304
      305 <h3>Configuration examples</h3>
      306 <pre><code># See everything and its status
      307 claude mcp list
      308
      309 # Turn a server off for the current project (interac
          tive)
      310 /mcp            # select server → Disable
      311
      312 # Local user-scope server (lives in ~/.claude.json →
           mcpServers)
      313 claude mcp add NAME --scope user -- npx -y some-mcp@
          latest --flag
      314 claude mcp remove NAME -s user
      315
      316 # claude.ai connectors: manage on claude.ai → Settin
          gs → Connectors.
      317 # Disconnecting there also removes them from the web
           app.
      318 # To keep them on the web but not in the terminal, d
          isable them per project with /mcp.</code></pre>
      319
      320 <h3>How to trim it</h3>
      321 <ol>
      322 <li>In a fresh session, run <code>/mcp</code> and di
          sable claude.ai connectors you don't use from the te
          rminal. Good candidates: Airtable, Canva, Lovable, I
          ndeed, vidIQ, Google Slides.</li>
      323 <li>Decide on <code>claude-terminal</code>: it's the
           largest single block of names (~150). If you don't
          control Claude Terminal.app from inside sessions, di
          sable it.</li>
      324 <li>Keep Engram, context7, and anything you actively
           use in the terminal.</li>
      325 </ol>

      353
      354 <h3>Why <code>~/CLAUDE.md</code> matters most</h3>
      355 <p>Claude Code reads <code>CLAUDE.md</code> from the
           session folder <em>and every parent folder</em>. Yo
          ur home folder is a parent of almost everything, so
          the Ruflo guide in <code>~/CLAUDE.md</code> loads in
           every session, whether you're editing music metadat
          a or reviewing a video config. It also <b>tells the
          model to use Ruflo tools</b> (swarms, <code>npx @cla
          ude-flow/cli</code> commands, "spawn ALL agents in O
          NE message"). With Ruflo off, those instructions are
           now dead weight that pushes in the wrong direction.
          </p>
      356 <p>It also conflicts with your own global rules: <co
          de>~/.claude/CLAUDE.md</code> says "do NOT route rou
          tine work through agents", while <code>~/CLAUDE.md</
          code> says to spawn swarms for 3+ files.</p>
      357
      358 <h3>How to trim it (reversible, versioned)</h3>
      359 <pre><code># Rename so it no longer auto-loads, keep
          ing it as a versioned record
      360 mv ~/CLAUDE.md ~/CLAUDE.ruflo-v1.md
      361
      362 # Rollback
      363 mv ~/CLAUDE.ruflo-v1.md ~/CLAUDE.md
      364
      365 # Learning/explanatory output style (adds the ★ Insi
          ght boxes + its hook text)
      366 claude plugin disable learning-output-style@claude-p
          lugins-official
      367 # Rollback
      368 claude plugin enable learning-output-style@claude-pl
          ugins-official</code></pre>
      369 <p>Also remove the "Ruflo Integration (auto-generate
          d by ruflo init)" section at the bottom of <code>~/.
          claude/CLAUDE.md</code> (comment it out as history i
          f you prefer).</p>

      387 <h2 id="chrome">7. Chrome DevTools MCP with Opera</h
          2>
      388
      389 <p><a href="https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/chrome
          -devtools-mcp">chrome-devtools-mcp</a> is Google's M
          CP server that lets an agent control and inspect a C
          hromium browser through the DevTools Protocol (CDP),
           using Puppeteer. It officially supports Chrome. <b>
          Opera is built on Chromium</b> and speaks the same p
          rotocol, so it works when pointed at Opera's executa
          ble.</p>
      390
      391 <h3>Verified <span class="tag measured">measured</sp
          an></h3>
      392 <p>Opera 136 launched with a throwaway profile and r
          emote debugging, and answered the protocol handshake
          :</p>
      393 <pre><code>"Browser": "Chrome/152.0.7977.130"
      394 "Protocol-Version": "1.3"
      395 "User-Agent": "… HeadlessChrome/152.0.0.0 Safari/537
          .36 OPR/136.0.0.0"</code></pre>
      396
      397 <h3>Installed configuration</h3>
      398 <pre><code>claude mcp add chrome-devtools --scope us
          er \
      399   -e CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS=1 \
      400   -- npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest \
      401      --executable-path /Applications/Opera.app/Conte
          nts/MacOS/Opera \
      402      --isolated \
      403      --no-usage-statistics \
      404      --no-performance-crux \
      405      --no-category-memory</code></pre>
      406 <table>
      407 <tr><th>Flag</th><th>Why</th></tr>
      408 <tr><td><code>--executable-path …/Opera</code></td><
          td>Drive Opera instead of Chrome</td></tr>
      409 <tr><td><code>--isolated</code></td><td>Temporary pr
          ofile, deleted on close. The agent <b>never sees you
          r real Opera</b> cookies, history, logins, or VPN se
          ttings.</td></tr>
      410 <tr><td><code>--no-usage-statistics</code></td><td>U
          sage stats go to Google <b>by default</b>; this turn
          s that off</td></tr>
      411 <tr><td><code>--no-performance-crux</code></td><td>S
          tops sending traced URLs to Google's CrUX API</td></
          tr>
      412 <tr><td><code>--no-category-memory</code></td><td>Dr
          ops 14 heap-snapshot tools you're unlikely to need (
          fewer names in context)</td></tr>
      413 <tr><td><code>CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS=1
          </code></td><td>No periodic npm update checks</td></
          tr>
      414 </table>
      415
      416 <div class="mermaid">
      417 sequenceDiagram
      418   participant You
      419   participant CC as Claude Code
      420   participant MCP as chrome-devtools-mcp (npx)
      421   participant O as Opera (temp profile)
      422   You->>CC: "Open localhost:3000 and check the conso
          le"
      423   CC->>MCP: new_page(url)
      424   MCP->>O: launch Opera --user-data-dir=tmp (first u
          se only)
      425   MCP->>O: CDP: Target.createTarget
      426   CC->>MCP: list_console_messages
      427   MCP->>O: CDP: Runtime / Log events
      428   O-->>MCP: messages + source-mapped stacks
      429   MCP-->>CC: results
      430   Note over O: profile deleted when Opera closes
      431 </div>
      432

  ★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
  - Plugin agents get a prefix, so they don't clash with yours. An
    agent from a plugin is listed as voltagent-infra:devops-engineer.
    Your own devops-engineer and security-engineer in
    ~/.claude/agents stay separate, so there's no fight over which
    copy wins (the duplicate-name problem the guide found in
    _incoming/).
  - The cost is small. Each agent's description is about 200
    characters, with no example dialogues, so the 46 agents add
    roughly 3k tokens. That's less than the single
    feedback-synthesizer agent costs with its four examples.
  - Uninstalling is easy. A plugin can be turned off without deleting
    anything: claude plugin disable
    voltagent-lang@voltagent-subagents. That's the same reversible
    approach as today's Ruflo cleanup.
